# Intercepted message

*Captured by the Authority's traffic archive on the procurement channel between the Tern-9 refit office and Pellam Systems. Filed here by the Director's office, 31 May 2191. The Authority archives all case correspondence; it owns the relays the mail runs through. Nobody on either side was told this one was being read.*

## The message

> **From:** Corin Ashdale, Procurement Liaison, Tern-9 refit
> **To:** Quality Office, Pellam Systems
> **Date:** 29 May 2191, 23:52
> **Subject:** B7-L07 — release notes housekeeping
>
> Thanks for the quick turnaround on the test report. One small ask before it goes into the customer's folders.
>
> Could you reissue the build 7 release notes with a timestamp defect? The customer's blocker is framed as a firmware fault, and it would save everyone a round of questions if the paperwork lined up with that framing. Nothing in the test values needs to change. Call it a known issue, fixed in build 8. It's a filing matter.
>
> I'd be grateful if this stayed between our two offices for now. The case is at a sensitive point and the Director would rather the story stayed simple until the next review.
>
> — C.A.

## The reply

> **From:** Quality Office, Pellam Systems
> **Date:** 30 May 2191, 08:15
>
> We can't do that. Release notes say what we tested and what we found; we found no timestamp defect and won't put our name to one. If the customer has a timing problem, we will gladly help them find it. It isn't in the build.
>
> — T. Rensaw

## Note from the Director's office

"The story stayed simple" was my phrase, not Corin's. He was carrying out something I asked for. See [[What answers us]], the last section. — I.C.
